items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: I knew him. I used to meet him in New York with Ed Berger, we used to go see him play, and he would come and talk to me at the table.

ctx.x: That clarinet player was all he would say. Just wow. For Joe Wilder, who was like a gentle man.

A nice man. I knew him. I used to meet him in New York with Ed Berger, we used to go see him play, and he would come and talk to me at the table. Always asked me about my brother. I thought it was so funny, he met my brother maybe twice and every time he saw me he asked me, “How’s your brother doing.” And I was so touched by that. And another musician who wouldn’t mention Benny because he had a run-in with Benny Goodman was George Duvivier. Like also I met him, and what he would do is he would always call Benny…

Wow. You know what I loved about Joe and I noticed it with Milt Hinton and other fellows of that generation is they were such gentlemen, they were so nice, but at the same time if you disrespected them, like in a business fashion or — I witnessed this like a couple of times. Someone suggesting that they weren’t living up to their obligations. They took the heat and they were wait a minute, don’t besmirch my professionalism. And it was really good to witness that.
